ok.displayName: OK Green (traffic light; same ink as the accent)

display.purpose: The rank readout (#3 of 144) in the rank head; the only size above 14px.

title.purpose: Uppercase section headings, day heads and offering group labels in secondary text.

body.purpose: Default for codes, times, values and labels; tabular numerals and slashed zero on.

body-prose.purpose: Help paragraphs, the about block, banners, empty state, criterion direction lines; distinguished from data by size and leading, not by family.

label.purpose: 10px uppercase tracked keys: readout keys, results column heads, about-block dt keys, the REGISTER label.

fonts.note: --sans is an alias of --mono; there is no second family.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: The :focus-within halo on a text field. Not elevation.

shadows.name: moved-ring
shadows.purpose: Inset ring on a result row that just moved after a re-rank; animates to transparent over 1400ms.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for every transition and the moved-row animation.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Colour state changes: background, border-color, color, opacity, switch knob, drag-row states.

motion.name: t-med
motion.purpose: Position changes: criterion row transform, course block transform and opacity.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: The wordmark cursor; the one authored motion in the world.

motion.name: block-hover
motion.purpose: Hover on a hued grid block, which cannot step up a tonal surface.

motion.name: moved
motion.purpose: Inset ring fade on a re-ranked result row.

motion.name: copied
motion.purpose: How long the Copy button stays in its primary 'Copied' state.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transition and animation durations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, including the cursor blink.

focusRing.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring; :focus alone is suppressed. Grid blocks use the same ring at 0 offset.

breakpoints.name: two-column
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: results panel drops below the grid as a 320px row; left panel narrows to 300px.

breakpoints.name: one-column
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: single column, page scrolls, results panel 420px tall, grid axis 38px, blocks reduce to code only, wordmark text and cursor hidden.

components.name: Prompt Field

components.css: .ds-about { width: 292px; padding: 6px 8px 8px; font: 400 11.5px/1.55 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1, 'zero' 1; color: var(--text-2, #98a797); } .ds-about p { margin: 0; } .ds-desc.ds-clamp { display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 4; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; } .ds-more { display: block; background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; font-size: 11px; color: var(--accent, #4ee38a); margin-top: 2px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-more:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 3px; } .ds-more:focus { outline: none; } .ds-more:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-ring, rgb(78 227 138 / 0.55)); outline-offset: 1px; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-about dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 2px 10px; margin: 8px 0 0; } .ds-about dt { font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--text-3, #778a7e); padding-top: 2px; } .ds-about dd { margin: 0; font-size: 11px; color: var(--text-2, #98a797); overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-about dd a { display: block; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--accent, #4ee38a); text-decoration: none; } .ds-about dd a:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
A single-user tool a CMU student opens at night, at registration time, to find the exact lecture and section codes to enter. The world is the category standard for a scheduler (inputs left, Monday-to-Friday grid centre, ranked list right) rendered as a terminal: near-black glass in four steps, 1px hairlines, one phosphor green, and a single monospace voice. The green is the terminal's ink: it is the caret, the $ prompt in the course field, the blinking cursor after the wordmark, the focus ring, the primary action, the lead criterion, the selected result and the "on" state of any control. Semantic status borrows the macOS traffic lights (red, amber, and the same green as "ok"). Course identity is carried by eight saturated ANSI hues (cyan, magenta, yellow, orange, purple, red, blue, green), the colours a terminal theme would print, applied as 16% fills with the hue at full strength for text.

There is one typeface. JetBrains Mono carries every string in the interface, codes and sentences alike; --sans exists only as an alias of --mono so legacy class hooks resolve to the same face. Prose is distinguished from data by size and leading (11–11.5px / 1.5–1.55 in secondary or tertiary text) rather than by a second family. Density is high and even: body 12.5px, controls 28px tall, list rows 26–44px, section padding 14px. Depth is tonal, never cast: surfaces step up by lightness and hairlines separate regions; the only box-shadows in the build are the 3px soft halo on a focused field and the fading inset ring on a just-moved result row.

Motion is short and eased out hard (120ms / 200ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) and used for state only, with two exceptions: the wordmark's cursor blinks on a 1.1s stepped cycle, the one authored motion in the world, and the results list re-sorting in place when the ranking order changes, where moved rows carry a 1px inset green ring that fades over 1.4s.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only (color-scheme: dark, no light theme); four near-black glass surfaces plus three hairline tones, all faintly cool with a green-grey text ramp.
One typeface: JetBrains Mono 400/500/600 for everything, tabular numerals and slashed zero on by default; no sans-serif anywhere.
One accent (phosphor green) for prompt, cursor, caret, selection, lead, primary action, focus and "on"; it is also the "ok" status colour.
Traffic-light semantics: red / amber / green as 14% tints with the full colour as text and icon.
Eight saturated ANSI course hues as hsl() triplets, applied as 16% fill / 45% border / 100% text.
Flat, hairline-bordered surfaces; no gradients (except the loading shimmer), no cast shadows, no blur.
Short eased-out transitions; motion only as a response to state, plus the blinking cursor.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Phosphor green is the terminal's ink and marks exactly these things: the prompt and cursor, what is selected, what leads, the primary action, focus, and "on". It is never used for decoration, headings, or icons at rest.

rules.name: The Tint-Plus-Ink Rule
rules.body: Status and course colours never fill a surface at full strength. The fill is the colour at 13–16% alpha; the text is the colour at 100%. The only solid colour fills in the world are the primary button, the lead priority badge, the checked switch track and the cursor.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by 1px hairline borders, never by shadow, gradient, or a change of more than one surface step.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Every string in the interface is JetBrains Mono. Prose is distinguished from data by size, leading and text tone, never by a second family. Do not reintroduce a sans-serif.

rules.name: The Twelve-and-a-Half Rule
rules.body: Body is 12.5px. Everything else is within 9–15px; nothing is larger than the rank display at 15px.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts. Hover lifts a surface by one tonal step (or brightens a hued block); focus draws a ring; selection tints. If a future popover needs separation it must earn it with a hairline and a surface step first.

dos: Do keep controls at 28px (24px small, selects and number inputs) with a 6px (4px small) radius and a 1px hairline-strong border; hover is one tonal step up, not a transform.
Do set every string in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals; mark prose by dropping to 11–11.5px with 1.5–1.55 leading in secondary or tertiary text.
Do reserve phosphor for prompt, cursor, selection, lead, primary action, focus and "on"; the lead criterion and selected result are the only green-filled rows on screen.
Do build status and course colour as a 13–16% tint fill with the full-strength colour as text and (for course blocks) a 45% border.
Do separate regions with 1px hairline borders and surface steps; wells sit one step below their panel on glass-floor.
Do use the standard ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) at 120ms for colour state and 200ms for position; honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do draw icons as 16-unit line paths at 1.5 stroke with round caps, rendered at 12–14px; inline the same drawing as a data URI where a background image is the only option (the select chevron).
Do make anything clickable a real <button> with an aria-label and the shared focus ring, as the grid blocks are.
donts: Don't add box-shadows, gradients, blur or glows; the only halo in the world is the 3px focus halo on a field and the only gradient is the loading shimmer.
Don't introduce a light theme or theme switch; the world is color-scheme: dark only.
Don't fill a surface with a status or course colour at full strength; solid fills belong to the primary button, the lead badge, the checked switch and the cursor.
Don't reintroduce Inter or any sans-serif; one face is the terminal's whole voice.
Don't use a second accent or a hue-coded heading; headings are 11px uppercase mono in secondary text.
Don't set text above 15px or below 9px; the type world lives between 9px corner marks and the 15px rank display.
Don't add authored motion beyond the cursor blink and the moved-row ring; everything else animates only as a response to state.
Don't replace drawn line icons with glyph fonts, emoji or an icon package.
